request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period, with listed milestones through 2027
deliverables: Not-for-profit entity establishment or host-organization agreement, transition architecture and migration plan, and public usage dashboard in Q3 2026
Board election via on-chain voting under published rules in Q4 2026
Transition of public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod to the new stack and transfer of Blockfrost intellectual property in Q1 2027
Public sustainability consultation and proposal in Q2-Q3 2027
Sustained operations with minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA, public dashboard verification, and quarterly technical and budget reports in 2027
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition through the proposed governance and contract structure
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano and fund 18 months of transition and operations.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own infrastructure or node.
The proposal states that Blockfrost was founded in 2020 by Five Binaries and joined IOG in 2024 with the goal of decentralizing it.
The proposal cites Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey links showing Blockfrost hosted-service usage rising from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal states that last month Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal states that 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the commercial model difficult for funding public-good operations.
The proposal commits to transferring Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to a governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.
The proposed not-for-profit board would have five seats, including four open-source infrastructure development entity seats and one community seat, with a preliminary board named in the document.
The requested budget is 9,832,979 ADA for 18 months, equivalent to 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, allocated mainly to staffing, operations and infrastructure, and legal/accounting costs.
The proposal states that unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and that quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

summary: The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA to transition Blockfrost into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with milestones covering entity setup, board election, service transition, IP transfer, sustainability planning, uptime commitments, dashboards, and quarterly reporting.
